1.  Checkpoint a database - SQLite
    The sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 (D,X,M,L,C) interface runs a checkpoint operation on database X of database connection D in mode M. Status information is written back into integers pointed to by L and C.

2.  Write-Ahead Logging - SQLite
    An application can initiate a checkpoint using any writable database connection on the database simply by invoking sqlite3_wal_checkpoint () or sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 ().

5.  How to manually perform checkpoint in SQLite android?

6.  SQLite WAL Internals — Frame Format, wal-index, Checkpoints, and ...
    SQLite Write-Ahead Logging WAL is the protocol that makes a SQLite database with multiple concurrent readers and a single writer behave like a real concurrent database. Set PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL once and reads stop blocking writes; writes stop blocking reads. The mechanism is a separate append-only log file, a tiny shared-memory index, and a checkpoint process that periodically folds the log ...

8.  SQLite WAL mode: how it works, checkpoints and tuning
    In WAL mode SQLite appends every change to a -wal file and leaves the main database file alone until a checkpoint copies those pages back. Readers find the right version of each page through an index held in a memory-mapped -shm file.

10.  GitHub - GreyforgeLabs/sqlite-checkpoint: Atomic SQLite WAL checkpoint ...
    SQLite databases in WAL mode accumulate changes in a write-ahead log. Long-running applications need a reliable way to flush that log and create consistent backups without stopping writes. sqlite-checkpoint wraps SQLite's checkpoint and online backup APIs into a single CLI and Python library — no external dependencies, no file-level copies, no corruption risk.
    github.com/GreyforgeLabs/sqlite-checkpoint
